items.title: Penang beats 25 cities worldwide as cheapest base for digital nomads
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Penang has been named the world’s most budget-friendly city for digital nomads in an international study covering 26 cities across 15 countries. The study by digital marketing agency Click Intelligence, published in Moneywise last month, placed Penang first with an overall score of 0.78, Berita Harian reported today. Penang Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said the international recognition reflected the state’s growing appeal as a destination of choice for digital nomads and international visitors.

items.title: How Trump could interfere in US midterm elections
items.summary: WASHINGTON: State officials who run US elections are bracing for further intervention by President Donald Trump's administration in next week's midterms, fearing federal authorities could disrupt voting, challenge ballot counts or try to block unfavourable results. Trump, whose Republicans face an uphill battle to retain control of Congress, has repeatedly questioned the integrity of US elections and urged his party to "nationalise" voting in at least 15 places. Pressure on officials: The Justice Department has warned election officials in every state that they could face prosecution if they knowingly allow non-citizens to vote.

items.title: GIIB shares extend losses amid heavy selling
items.summary: The rubber compounds manufacturer's shares fell to a morning low of 24 sen before recovering to 33 sen as at 9.53am, still down 21 sen or 38.89 per cent from Thursday's close of 54 sen. On Thursday, the stock plunged 23.94 per cent from 71 sen to 54 sen, wiping RM140.5 million off its market capitalisation, which fell to RM446.2 million from RM586.7 million. At 33 sen, the stock was down 41 sen, or 55.41 per cent, from that peak.

items.title: Malaysia’s inflation eases to 1.8pc in September, govt monitors global cost pressures
items.summary: Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the government was nevertheless keeping a close watch on developments amid rising global fuel prices and production cost pressures, BuletinTV3 reported. He said global crude oil prices had surged to US$116.80 (RM472.75) per barrel from US$90.90 in August, while Malaysia’s Producer Price Index (PPI) also rose to 12 per cent in September 2026 from 10.7 per cent the previous month. “The government is continuing the implementation of Budi Madani RON95 (BUDI95), maintaining the subsidised RON95 price at RM1.99 per litre, as well as Budi Madani Diesel (Budi Diesel) for eligible recipients.

items.title: Netanyahu bloc finishes ahead in Israel vote, but well short of majority
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's camp finished ahead of the opposition but remained well short of a majority, final results from Israel's general election showed on Friday, setting the stage for tough coalition talks or potentially another vote. Netanyahu's coalition of right-wing and far-right parties won 53 of the Knesset's 120 seats, with his Likud party remaining the largest faction with 27 seats. Netanyahu's Likud party said on Thursday.

items.title: PKR urges Umno not to mislead public over rural road projects
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 30 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) has urged Umno not to mislead the public about the Ministry of Finance’s (MoF) directive to postpone the issuance of new Letters of Acceptance (SST) for rural road projects. PKR deputy secretary-general Saifuddin Shafi Muhammad stressed that deferring the SST is not the same as cancelling rural development projects, as alleged by Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki. “Do not conflate the deferral of the SST for rural road projects with allegations of a wholesale cancellation of road, water supply and electricity projects.

items.title: Teen rallies take to the streets across Italy
items.summary: ROME: School and university students are set to rally in several Italian cities on Friday to call for more funding for schools and support for housing, with security forces preparing for possible clashes. "On Friday, we expect a massive mobilisation of students, who will block and empty schools," Laura Teresi, 18, from Rome's Cavour high school and a spokesperson for the OSA student movement, told AFP. The students will also protest against the "endless budget cuts to teaching", Teresi said.

items.title: PKR urges Melaka voters to weigh track record, plans before casting ballots
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 30 — The 16th Melaka State Election gives voters a chance to assess each party’s track record and offers when choosing the state’s leadership, said Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) deputy communications director Jonathan Vela. He said voters should consider how parties plan to fulfil their campaign commitments. “Ahead of the Melaka State Election, Pakatan Harapan’s (PH) theme ‘Melaka Rumah Kita’ reflects the aspiration to build a better future for the state through joint efforts and prioritising the people’s welfare,” he said.

items.title: Azalina: Govt open to considering release of full report on Azam Baki shareholding probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The government is prepared to consider a recommendation to release the full report of a special committee investigating allegations concerning former Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Tan Sri Azam Baki’s shareholding. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said disclosure would be considered if necessary and subject to appropriate deliberations, Berita Harian reported. She said any decision would have to take into account existing legal provisions, particularly those concerning the protection of personal information, confidentiality of investigation documents and records of asset declarations, as well as the interests of relevant parties.

items.title: Sabah police cripple armed gang behind 17 luxury house break-ins involving RM304,500 in losses
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 30 — Sabah police have crippled an armed syndicate linked to 17 gang robbery and luxury house-breaking cases involving RM304,500 in losses across several districts since early this year, said Sabah Police Commissioner Datuk Jauteh Dikun. He said the breakthrough was achieved through two special operations, Op Casa and Op Pintu, following the formation of a special task force in September to investigate two armed robberies reported in the state capital in August. “Police also seized various valuables, including luxury watches, designer handbags, electronic devices, cars, fishing equipment, and a safe box.

items.title: Penang tops global ranking for budget-friendly digital nomad living
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang has been ranked the world's most budget-friendly city for digital nomads in a new international study covering 26 cities across 15 countries. The study, conducted by digital marketing agency Click Intelligence and featured in Moneywise in October, placed Penang first with an overall score of 0.78. Penang Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said the international recognition reflected the state's growing appeal as a destination for digital nomads and international visitors.

items.title: Budget 2027 passes policy stage; committee debate from Nov 2 as govt mulls tighter GLC rules, 1MDB recovery
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The Supply (Budget) Bill 2027, which was passed at the policy stage following a two-week debate, stood out as a key development during this week’s Dewan Rakyat session as the proceedings also covered a range of other issues, including administrative governance, national development, and public welfare. Budget 2027, tabled by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on October 9, secured the approval of the majority of Dewan Rakyat members on Thursday which allows the Bill to proceed to the committee stage, which is scheduled to take place from November 2 to November 26. said Minister of Finance II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.

items.title: BTH: Sugar Babies: Where does consent end and exploitation begin? [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sugar baby arrangements do not automatically constitute criminal conduct, but those involving coercion, exploitation or sexual services may cross legal boundaries, a criminologist has warned. Speaking on this week's Beyond the Headlines, criminologist Dr Haezreena Begum Abdul Hamid said authorities must assess the circumstances of each case, as financial assistance between consenting adults does not, by itself, amount to solicitation or prostitution. Haezreena also warned that financial dependence could become a means of control, with seemingly consensual relationships escalating into manipulation, pressure to engage in unwanted sexual activities, blackmail or extortion.

items.title: Bersatu confirms use of own logo in Melaka state election
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 30 — Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) will use its official party logo in the 16th Melaka State Election on November 14, said its secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali. Mohamed Azmin, who is also the party election director, said he had sent an official letter to the Election Commission (EC) last week regarding the confirmation of the party’s logo usage in the state election. “We will use the Bersatu logo.

items.title: Perikatan delays naming candidate for one Melaka state seat, denies allocation dispute
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 30 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) has postponed announcing its candidate for one remaining state seat allocated to the coalition under an understanding with Barisan Nasional (BN) for the 16th Melaka state election. Its chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar said the delay was due to several outstanding matters, not a lack of qualified candidates. Asked whether the delay stemmed from disputes over seat allocations among coalition component parties, Ahmad Samsuri said this was not the case.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia slips after higher opening
items.summary: Among heavyweight stocks, Maybank rose two sen to RM10.02, while CIMB gained seven sen to RM6.96 and IHH Healthcare added four sen to RM7.89. In active trade, Zetrix AI and JAKS Resources shed one sen each to seven sen and 14 sen, respectively. GIIB Holdings fell 10.5 sen to 43.5 sen, while Ni Hsin and EWI Capital gained one sen each to 38 sen and 14.5 sen, respectively.

items.title: One held as Kelantan police open three investigation papers over extreme social media comments
items.summary: TUMPAT, Oct 30 — Police have opened three investigation papers in relation to extreme comments on social media related to enforcement issues that are alleged to threaten public order and tarnish the image of the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM). Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said a male suspect has been detained in relation to this case, whereas two other cases are under investigation and the suspects have been identified. Mohd Yusoff said that this number of arrests was compared to 59 individuals in 2025 and 51 in 2024.

items.title: Melaka polls: Perikatan names five candidates
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 30 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) has announced five candidates for the 16th Melaka state election next month. The names of the candidates were announced by PN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar at Dewan Muallim Haji Abdul Wahid in Bukit Katil here last night. PN’s candidates for the Melaka state election are as follows: N.13 Paya Rumput - Rafie Ahmad N.16 Ayer Keroh - Datuk Seri Michael Gan N.17 Bukit Katil - Ridzuan Sarif N.19 Kesidang - Albert Kok N.24 Bemban - Dr Mohd Yadzil Yaakub The Melaka state legislative assembly was dissolved on September 23, and the Election Commission (EC) has set November 14 as polling day, with nomination day on October 31 and early voting on November 10.

items.title: Indonesian drought could lift Malaysian planters
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian plantation companies could benefit from firmer crude palm oil (CPO) prices in 2027 as worsening drought conditions in Indonesia threaten to tighten regional supply. Singapore-listed Wilmar is one of the world's largest oil palm plantation groups. "Wilmar's weaker Indonesian palm oil output outlook reinforces concerns about drought-related supply risks extending into 2027, supporting our constructive crude palm oil view," CIMB Securities said.

items.title: PAS’ Tuan Ibrahim claims Pakatan fears BN-Perikatan unity ahead of Melaka polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is deeply wary of the unity between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) in the upcoming Melaka state election, PAS deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man claimed. He said the cooperation could deliver a major victory for the coalition, Sinar Harian reported today. Tuan Ibrahim also urged party machinery members to set aside petty issues throughout the campaigning period and not be influenced by agendas pursued by certain parties.

items.title: Binance's possible hack triggers US$3 billion freeze in crypto assets
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said on Thursday it had frozen US$3 billion in crypto assets as it investigated a potential security breach, with stablecoin issuers Circle and Tether also freezing related assets. "Binance will cover all hacking losses," Binance co-founder Yi He said, without providing further details about the incident. Tether said it had frozen nearly US$1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than US$800 million.

items.title: Damaged concrete pipe behind Bayan Baru sinkhole, road closed for repairs until Nov 7, says Penang exco
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 30 — Damage to a 750-millimetre concrete pipe has been identified as the cause of a sinkhole on Mayang Pasir Highway in Bayan Baru near here, with repair works expected to be completed by November 7. Penang Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said Indah Water Konsortium (IWK) Sdn Bhd was carrying out repairs in stages to ensure safety at the site. Motorists have been advised to use alternative routes via Lebuh Mayang Pasir, Jalan Mahsuri and Lorong Mayang Pasir 1.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng says SMEs oppose mandatory EPF contributions for foreign workers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng has urged the government to exempt existing foreign workers from mandatory Employees Provident Fund (EPF) contributions and a proposed RM300 monthly minimum wage increase, saying the measures would impose additional costs on local businesses, particularly micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). The DAP lawmaker said he had told Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim that employers, including MSMEs, were opposed to the mandatory contributions and the increase in minimum wages for existing foreign workers. Lim asked why foreign domestic workers were exempt from the mandatory 2 per cent EPF contribution despite also being foreign workers.

items.title: Man dies after car swept away by floodwaters in Rembau; separate rescue saves Indonesian man, says Fire Dept
items.summary: Rembau Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) senior operations commander Mohamad Khairul Yahaya said it received an emergency call from the victim’s son at 9.20pm. “The rescue team, with assistance from the Water Rescue Team (PPDA) from the Teluk Kemang BBP, managed to extricate the victim, who was trapped inside the car, about half an hour later. He said the rescue operation, which involved 13 personnel, including two senior officers from the Rembau and Teluk Kemang fire and rescue stations, ended at 10pm.

items.title: Norhizam unfazed by 'pig-shooting assemblyman' label
items.summary: MELAKA: Former Pengkalan Batu assemblyman Datuk Norhizam Hassan Baktee is unfazed by the nicknames he earned during his previous tenure, including "YB Beliau" and the "pig-shooting assemblyman", as he prepares to return to public service. The 60-year-old Bersatu candidate said the labels were simply part of his experience as a people's representative, particularly his willingness to go to the ground and address residents' problems. Which assemblyman would dare to go out and shoot wild boars?

items.title: Petronas’ continued role as MotoGP main sponsor up for discussion, says Zahid
items.summary: BANGI, Oct 30 — The proposal to ensure that Petronas remains the main sponsor of MotoGP in the coming years will be discussed with the president and Group chief executive officer of Petronas, Tan Sri Tengku Muhammad Taufik Tengku Aziz. “I met Carmelo, and he offered Petronas the opportunity to continue as a sponsor of MotoGP. Ahmad Zahid said that although sponsorship costs might be high, several alternative approaches could be explored to ensure Petronas remains MotoGP’s main organiser and sponsor in the coming years.

items.title: Mi Technovation poised for strong year-end finish
items.summary: The stronger-than-expected results prompted Public Investment Bank Bhd (PublicInvest) to raise its earnings forecasts for the semiconductor equipment and materials manufacturer. PublicInvest said the group's core net profit surged 73 per cent year-on-year to RM152 million in the first nine months of the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026 (FY26). Mi Technovation's semiconductor materials business remained its main earnings contributor, generating more than RM100 million in earnings during the nine-month period.

items.title: Azalina: Govt open to releasing full report on Azam Baki's shareholding
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is open to making public the full report of a special committee that investigated allegations of share ownership involving former Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Tan Sri Azam Baki, subject to legal considerations. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said disclosure would be considered if necessary. "The issue of ownership and asset declarations, including Azam's shareholding, has been examined by the Special Investigation Committee established on Feb 13.

items.title: Amazon burns cash, Intel flags weak PC demand as AI boom's costs ripple across markets
items.summary: Amazon's shares fell 7 per cent in after-hours trading, accompanied by losses of between 5.8 and 6.7 per cent in AI cloud stocks CoreWeave, Nebius and Iren. Alphabet, which closed regular trading nearly 13 per cent lower, fell another 1.5 per cent after hours. Shares of PC makers HP and Dell fell 8 per cent and 6.8 per cent, respectively.

items.title: Ministry targets year-end rollout of revised abandoned vehicle guidelines
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Housing and Local Government Ministry is studying the need to improve existing legal provisions to address the issue of abandoned vehicles. The approach, he said, aims to shift the management of abandoned vehicles from a purely enforcement model to a comprehensive solution balancing legal authority, public rights, and owners' social responsibility. "The ministry is also improving the Guidelines for the Management of Abandoned Vehicles in Local Authority Operational Areas introduced in 2020.

items.title: Govt plans to reform development expenditure allocation based on states’ needs, says Economy Ministry
items.summary: The Economy Ministry said the main focus was to trim the productivity gap between less-developed states and the national average. “Annual increases in allocations under Budget 2027 do not necessarily mean that states receiving smaller allocations are underperforming compared with more developed states. The Economy Ministry said structural economic imbalances between states posed a threat to national competitiveness.

items.title: Gold prices edge lower as US inflation data reinforces Fed outlook
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Gold prices eased in early Asian trade on Friday after falling more than one per cent in the previous session, as persistent US inflation fuelled expectations of further Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hikes, weighing on bullion. FUNDAMENTALS Spot gold fell 0.4 per cent to US$4,006.06 an ounce by 0036 GMT, while US gold futures for December delivery dropped 0.3 per cent to US$4,018.50. Spot silver fell one per cent to US$51.87 an ounce, platinum was steady at US$1,488.00, while palladium declined 0.5 per cent to US$1,000.75.

items.title: Rural Roads Programme financing prioritised, 2026 allocation rises to RM3.1b, says Amir Hamzah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The government is prioritising the Rural Roads Programme (JALB) project financing with the total allocation for 2026 rising to RM3.1 billion from the original allocation of RM2.11 billion, according to the Finance Ministry (MoF). Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the nearly RM1 billion in additional allocation comprises the additional RM500 million for the Rural and Regional Development Ministry (KKDW) and the earlier Notice of Change (NOC) worth RM491 million made by KKDW. Amir Hamzah said the actual expenditure for JALB projects from 2018 to 2022 amounted to RM3.72 billion, while actual expenditure and allocations for the 2023-2027 period reached RM11 billion.

items.title: Anwar tells Transport Ministry, Rapid KL to act on train overcrowding complaints
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed Transport Minister Anthony Loke to urgently address overcrowding on train services, warning that the problem could disrupt the daily routines of commuters. “This (train overcrowding) happens frequently and it certainly disrupts the daily routines of the wider public. Could we have more train carriages, please?

items.title: Iran says four tankers on fire after hitting mines in Hormuz
items.summary: TEHERAN: Four tankers caught fire after hitting mines while attempting to navigate the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's armed forces said on Thursday, a day after the US military said it had cleared key routes through the waterway. "Over the past 24 hours, three violating oil tankers exploded and caught fire after striking mines while attempting to pass through the unauthorised southern route of the Strait of Hormuz," Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) said in a statement. Later on Thursday, Iran's army reported that another tanker had caught fire east of the strait after hitting mines while "operating in a restricted and dangerous area".

items.title: Too many good companies stay small for too long: Anwar urges Bursa Malaysia to help more local firms become regional champions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called on Bursa Malaysia Bhd to help more Malaysian companies grow into regional champions, saying too many promising businesses remain small for too long. “I would like to see more mid-tier companies grow, list and become regional champions. Second Finance Minister Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan, Bursa Malaysia chairman Tan Sri Abdul Farid Alias, Bursa Malaysia chief executive officer Datuk Fad’l Mohamed and Securities Commission Malaysia chairman Datuk Mohammad Faiz Azmi were also present.

items.title: Kuala Pilah floods displace 38, including nine senior citizens
items.summary: KUALA PILAH: A temporary flood relief centre was opened at Sekolah Kebangsaan Undang Johol last night after two areas were hit by floods. The centre opened at 10.25pm to house 38 victims from 17 families from Rumah Rakyat Kuala Johol and Kampung Padang Jual, Johol. A Kuala Pilah Social Welfare Department spokesman said the centre was opened after the Johol state constituency headman reported rising floodwaters that had yet to recede in both locations.

items.title: Firecracker materials spark blaze at Gelang Patah fruit stall [WATCH]
items.summary: The Johor Fire and Rescue Department operations centre said it received an emergency call at 9.20pm. It said a team of seven personnel, led by Senior Fire Officer I Saifulizam Salleh from the Iskandar Puteri Fire and Rescue Station, rushed to the scene with a fire engine and arrived six minutes later. "Upon arrival at the scene, the operations team found a fire outside a fruit stall storing firecrackers.

items.title: Grieving Spain demands answers for latest rail disaster
items.summary: TOLEDO: Spain began demanding answers on Thursday after its second high-speed train collision this year killed 69 people and injured scores, as distraught relatives desperately sought news about their loved ones. One of Europe's deadliest rail disasters this century struck south of Madrid on Wednesday morning when a service operated by state operator Renfe ploughed into the back of a stationary train belonging to private Spanish company Iryo. Manuel San Emeterio, whose 54-year-old brother Pepe is missing, travelled to the central city of Toledo to provide DNA samples to the Civil Guard.

items.title: Four Melaka seats set for PH-Bersatu clashes
items.summary: MELAKA: Four state constituencies will see straight or multi-cornered contests between Pakatan Harapan and Bersatu in the Melaka election following the party's announcement of eight candidates last night. Bersatu secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali said the party was leaving it to Melaka voters to decide who deserved to represent them, despite the overlap in seat allocations with PH. The party's election director said Bersatu would continue to compete without resorting to smear tactics, instead offering policies focused on public welfare, economic growth and job creation.

items.title: Differing views among ministries part of healthy policy process, not disunity, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Differing views or approaches among ministries do not necessarily reflect division within the government, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said the government systematically coordinates between ministries to align policies, prevent overlapping functions, and ensure every decision is made based on public interest, national development priorities, and the government’s financial capacity. “To ensure effective governance, every government policy and decision must undergo proper deliberation and coordination.

items.title: Bank of Japan to hold rates, signal further hikes
items.summary: TOKYO: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) is set to keep interest rates steady on Friday but stress its focus on preventing underlying inflation from overshooting its two per cent target, suggesting scope to raise borrowing costs as soon as December. "Global price pressures from AI investment are quite strong, which means the recent inflation is partly demand driven," said Kazuo Momma, a former BOJ executive who is currently executive economist at Mizuho Research Institute. "By declaring that its policy phase has changed, the BOJ is essentially telling markets it will hike rates once a quarter," he said, predicting rate hikes in December and March next year.

items.title: ‘Which is more nerve-racking?’ Tengku Zafrul jokes about Syed Saddiq’s MoU signing with govt, wedding vows with Bella
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) chairman Datuk Seri Tengku Zafrul Abdul Aziz has poked fun at Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman, asking whether he was more nervous about exchanging wedding vows with actress Bella Astillah or signing a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the government. In an Instagram post yesterday, Tengku Zafrul said he had posed the question to Syed Saddiq, drawing a humorous comparison between the two commitments. The post followed the Madani government’s signing of an MoU with Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) and several other opposition MPs, including Syed Saddiq.

items.title: Bitcoin, cryptocurrency prices fall after Binance reports security issue
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Cryptocurrency prices fell on Friday after Binance reported a potential security issue and said more than US$2.5 billion in assets had been frozen. Bitcoin dropped to a six-week low of US$77,646, while ether fell to a two-month low of US$2,238.76. BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, fell more than 8 per cent over the past 24 hours to US$694, according to market aggregator CoinGecko.

items.title: Ringgit opens higher versus US dollar for 10 consecutive days
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit open higher for 10 consecutive trading days against the US dollar on Friday, reflecting continued positive sentiment in the local currency at the start of trading. At 8am, the ringgit edged up to 4.0570/0625 against the greenback from Friday's close of 4.0575/0620. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index (DXY) fell 0.33 per cent to 101.854 points.

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar directs Loke, Rapid KL to resolve recurring train congestion
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed Transport Minister Anthony Loke to immediately resolve train congestion issues that disrupt the daily routines of commuters. The prime minister's directive followed complaints by a Threads user, identified as siti.anisahj, about overcrowding at train station platforms last night. Earlier, siti.anisahj posted several photos showing the daily congestion faced by train commuters, especially in the capital.

items.title: 'Diabolical' Halloween festivities banned in Honduran towns
items.summary: TEGUCIGALPA: At least six municipalities in Honduras have banned Halloween celebrations this year on the grounds that they promote wickedness. Shopping centres must also "refrain from promoting and selling items" related to Halloween. The proposed ban would restrict "costume contests, decorations and recreational activities" related to Halloween.

items.title: The business of keeping people driven
items.summary: OWNING a business and working in one are two very different experiences. Every decision has consequences, and every setback can feel personal. It is simply a reality that effective leaders must understand.

items.title: Potential Maxis-U Mobile merger may squeeze earnings, dividends
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A merger between Maxis Bhd and U Mobile Sdn Bhd could weigh on both telcos in the near term, with higher 5G capital expenditure, weaker earnings and dividend pressures, said Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB). HLIB said a combination would reduce the market from three operators to two, adding that Maxis and U Mobile will form a subscriber base broadly on par with CelcomDigi Bhd. If the merger materialises, Maxis will gain U Mobile's nationwide 5G network, preserving network differentiation rather than converging to parity with CelcomDigi under Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB).

items.title: Govt ready to offer more incentives to steel manufacturers
items.summary: Malaysia's steel industry is valued at about RM35 billion, equivalent to 1.7 per cent of gross domestic product. Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Zin said manufacturers faced pricing pressure from imported steel, making it increasingly important to move beyond conventional products into higher-margin segments. Sim said manufacturers seeking to produce more sophisticated steel products could receive additional support, building on existing incentives such as pioneer status and investment tax allowances.

items.title: [UPDATED] Crypto platform Binance confirms major hack, more than US$2.5bil frozen
items.summary: NEW YORK: Cryptocurrency platform Binance said on Thursday that it had fallen victim to a major hack, resulting in the freezing of more than US$2.5 billion in an effort to prevent the assets from being stolen. The company — the world's largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes — said it had suspended trading on certain products. Circle chief Jeremy Allaire said his company had frozen more than US$800 million in USDC.

items.title: Australian mushroom murderer loses appeal
items.summary: MELBOURNE: Australian mushroom murderer Erin Patterson lost her bid to overturn her convictions on Friday, failing to prove that she was wrongfully jailed for killing three people with a poisoned lunch. Patterson was found guilty last year of murdering her husband's parents and elderly aunt after deliberately lacing their beef Wellington meal with highly toxic death cap mushrooms. The court ruled that Patterson's non-parole period should be set aside, meaning the 52-year-old is likely to die in prison.

items.title: Budget 2027: How much could pet owners save under the new pet tax relief?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Pet owners could soon claim tax relief on adoption, vaccination and sterilisation expenses under a proposal announced in Budget 2027. Instead of creating a separate allowance, the proposed relief would fall under the existing RM2,500 lifestyle tax relief limit. The actual tax savings would depend on eligible spending, the taxpayer's applicable income tax rate and how much of the relief limit remains unused.

items.title: Johor DOE probes Sungai Kim Kim after river turns white again, cable excavation suspected
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 29 — The Johor Department of Environment (DOE) is investigating allegations that Sungai Kim Kim in Pasir Gudang has become polluted again, turning white yesterday. Johor DOE director Dr Mohd Famey Yusoff said enforcement officers inspected the site at about 6pm following a complaint about the incident. Mohd Famey said preliminary investigations suggested that the incident could have been caused by a one-off waste discharge into the river.

items.title: Govt increases allocations to all states, Sabah and Sarawak receive highest sums, says Amir Hamzah
items.summary: Meanwhile, the allocation for the Malaysian Road Records Information System (MARRIS) increased to RM5.6 billion in 2026 from RM5.2 billion in 2023. Meanwhile, Amir Hamzah said the overall allocation for Sabah and Sarawak is the highest, increasing to RM18.7 billion and RM16.2 billion, respectively. Sabah’s RM18.7 billion allocation comprises RM8.9 billion for operating expenses, RM7 billion for development, and RM2.8 billion in grants to the state government.

items.title: MCA gets Bandar Hilir as third Melaka seat to contest, says Wee Ka Siong
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong said the party has been given an additional seat - Bandar Hilir - to contest in the Melaka State Election. He said Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) finalised the decision today, with MCA set to contest in three state constituencies, including Machap Jaya and Kelebang. Wee said its candidate for the Bandar Hilir state seat will be Melaka Historic City Council councillor Jasmine Lok Huey Yee, 38.

items.title: MACC issues asset declaration notices to businessman Nazir Hussin and brother
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) issued asset declaration notices to businessman Datuk Seri Nazir Hussin Akhtar Hussin and his brother, Datuk Mubarak Hussain, on October 20. Nazir Hussin was at the MACC Office in Putrajaya to receive the notice under Section 36(1)(a) of the MACC Act 2009, while Mubarak Hussain received the notice at his residence. When contacted, MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the matter, saying both individuals complied with the notices.

items.title: Finance minister II: GST not an option amid high cost of living, govt sticking with SST
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The federal government will continue to implement the Sales and Service Tax (SST), as the Goods and Services Tax (GST) will not be considered due to the ongoing burden of the cost of living. Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the government would continue to improve the SST to reduce the impact of cascading taxes and simplify compliance. “The government can choose which goods and services to tax while exempting essential items.

items.title: MOH to conduct special recruitment for 750 permanent medical officer posts in Sabah, Sarawak
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 29 — The Health Ministry (MOH) will conduct a special recruitment exercise to fill 750 permanent Medical Officer Grade UD10 vacancies in Sabah and Sarawak, with applications open from November 9 to 15. MOH said the recruitment is open to all contract-appointed medical officers who began their housemanship training from Series 1/2016 on December 5, 2016, to Series 6/2024 on October 14, 2024, including those whose service contracts had expired. The ministry said eligible and interested officers could submit their applications through the Public Service Commission’s SPA9 system when the recruitment advertisement opened.

items.title: Former Pahang water firm procurement manager begins three-year jail term after losing bribery appeal
items.summary: A three-member panel led by Justice Datuk Noorin Badaruddin ruled that Sani Khan Ali Khan had failed to show any error of law or material fact in the High Court decision that convicted him on all the charges. On January 26, the Kuantan High Court set aside a Sessions Court decision that had acquitted and discharged him of all the charges. In today’s proceedings, Justice Noorin said the High Court’s intervention was justified and that it had made no material error in setting aside the Sessions Court decision that had acquitted and discharged Sani Khan.
